title: Midpoint chain: Positive-ink invoice
topics: Linked lists, binary trees and search trees
summary: Find the middle node using fast and slow pointers, choosing the second middle for even-length lists. Produce values from that node to the tail; an empty head produces no values. Return the sum of strictly positive values in the derived sequence, or 0 when none exist.
descriptionMd:
A two-speed inspection wheel locates the second middle label of an even-length chain. Neri prepares an invoice that accepts only positive ink adjustments. Zero and negative derived readings stay off the invoice.

Find the middle node using fast and slow pointers, choosing the second middle for even-length lists. Produce values from that node to the tail; an empty head produces no values.

Return the sum of strictly positive values in the derived sequence, or 0 when none exist.

Implement midpointChainPositiveInkInvoice(head, k). k is part of the common inspection-card signature and does not affect this task's result.
unitIntro: Fast and slow pointers. Find the middle node using fast and slow pointers, choosing the second middle for even-length lists. Produce values from that node to the tail; an empty head produces no values. Keep the sequence order specified here before computing the requested receipt. A scan invariant says what has been processed and what remains. Work through the proof strip first, then change the returned summary without changing the definition of that sequence. The last card revisits loop accumulators from Hello, Keys.
constraints: 1 <= k <= 8. All arithmetic results fit a signed 32-bit integer.
Numeric readings lie between -1,000,000 and 1,000,000, subject to the task's shape and ordering rules.
Lists are acyclic. Trees use level-order JSON with null for missing children; [] is an empty root. The runner supplies nodes with val/next or val/left/right.

Target time O(n); auxiliary space including the derived sequence O(n). n is the input length; d distinct values; q query count; M maximum reading; V vertices; E edges; h tree height; r reported tree nodes.
hints: Start with fast and slow pointers. What state describes the portion you have already processed?

Find the middle node using fast and slow pointers, choosing the second middle for even-length lists. Produce values from that node to the tail; an empty head produces no values. Derive each required reading once; do not restart the whole procedure for every output position.
Return the sum of strictly positive values in the derived sequence, or 0 when none exist. Handle the empty derived sequence according to the stated return rule.

cases.explanation: The derived sequence is [7,0,12]. Return the sum of strictly positive values in the derived sequence, or 0 when none exist. This gives 19.
The derived sequence is [-2,4]. Return the sum of strictly positive values in the derived sequence, or 0 when none exist. This gives 4.
The derived sequence is []. Return the sum of strictly positive values in the derived sequence, or 0 when none exist. This gives 0.
